rows.statement: Power-conference programs send hundreds of scholarship offers per class (typically about 150 to 240, some over 400) to sign a class of about 20 to 27; that is roughly 6 to 10 offers per signee.

sources.citation: Ross Dellenger, Sports Illustrated, Recruiting's Biggest Bait-and-Switch: The Uncommittable Scholarship Offer (2019-02-05, https://www.si.com/college/2019/02/05/uncommittable-offers-recruiting-national-signing-day)
sources.quote: That's an average of about 237 offers per school per year

sources.citation: Dallas Morning News, Inside the dirty underbelly of college football recruiting's boom of non-committable offers (2019-02-01, republished 2019-07-15, https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2019/07/15/inside-dirty-underbelly-college-football-recruitings-boom-non-committable-offers-non-binding-promises)
sources.locator: 2018 and 2019 cycles, Texas Power Five programs
sources.quote: offered an average of about 144 scholarships, according to 247Sports.com

sources.citation: On3, Breaking down early 2025 offers nationally (Iowa team site, https://www.on3.com/teams/iowa-hawkeyes/news/breaking-down-early-2025-offers-nationally/)
sources.locator: table 2025 OFFERS, 70 Power programs (median 171.5, mean 186, range 33 to 461, computed from the table)
sources.quote: breaking down the number of scholarships each program has offered in the Class of 2025

rows.notes: Three independent publishers (SI and Dallas Morning News both count from 247Sports offer lists, On3 from its own database; treated as separate groups because each did its own count for a different year). SI 2020 (John Garcia Jr.) adds: more than half of the 65 Power programs at 150 or more offers for the 2021 class by February 2020. Class size: Dallas Morning News, 'signing just 20 to 30 players a year'. The game already holds offers per signee as front-office college.offersPerSignee 8.5 and league offer.perPlaceTop 8. rows.statement: A program's recruiting board holds about 500 names at the start of a cycle for about 25 places, about 20 names per place, so a staff evaluates roughly two names for every offer it sends.

sources.citation: Lance O's Recruiting Network, The Recruiting Board: How College Coaches Rank 500 Prospects for 25 Roster Spots (2026-11-21, https://www.lanceosrecruitingnetwork.com/post/the-recruiting-board-how-college-coaches-rank-500-prospects-for-25-roster-spots)
sources.quote: A typical program might have 500 names on that board at the start of a cycle.

rows.notes: FLAGGED, 1 of 3: only one page states a board size, and it is a commercial recruiting service blog. Context read the same day, not the same number so not counted: Athlon Sports 2014 (Penn State coordinator 'has already watched film of 150 safeties in the Class of 2015', one position); IMG Academy (master lists 800 to 8,000, evaluation lists of 20 to 300 athletes, all sports); SI 2025 (Tommy Reamon Jr.: 'For a single spot, a staff might offer eight, nine, even 10 players'). The ratio of two names per offer (500 names against the 237 offer average of F-recruiting-practice-0001) is this thread's arithmetic. Owed: a staff interview or program document stating board size.
